title: Impact of CT-Based Bone Density on the Risk of Pedicle Screw Loosening Following Lumbar Posterior Spinal Fusion: A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary:
Background: Posterior lumbar spinal fusion using pedicle screw–rod instrumentation is an established surgical procedure for the treatment of both degenerative and traumatic disorders of the spine. Despite advances in surgical techniques and implant technology, pedicle screw loosening remains a clinically relevant postoperative complication that may be associated with pain, functional impairment, pseudarthrosis, and the need for revision surgery.
The stability of pedicle screw fixation is largely determined by the quality of the surrounding trabecular bone. Reduced bone quality, particularly in patients with osteoporosis, may compromise the primary stability of the implant and increase the risk of long-term screw loosening.
In recent years, the assessment of bone quality using Hounsfield unit (HU) measurements obtained from routinely acquired CT scans has become an established method for the opportunistic evaluation of bone mineral density. Several studies have demonstrated a significant correlation between HU values and established techniques for measuring bone mineral density, particularly dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and quantitative computed tomography (QCT). Furthermore, low HU values have consistently been associated with an increased risk of instrumentation-related complications following spinal fusion surgery. A recent systematic review and meta-analysis including 35 studies and 3,927 patients confirmed the prognostic value of preoperative HU measurements for predicting the occurrence of such complications.
The aim of the present study is to identify radiographic predictors of pedicle screw loosening following posterior lumbar pedicle screw–rod instrumentation involving up to three spinal motion segments. Particular emphasis will be placed on the predictive value of preoperative CT-based bone density.

Hypothesis: Reduced CT-based bone density is an independent predictor of postoperative pedicle screw loosening.

Assessment of CT-Based Bone Density: Bone quality will be assessed using Hounsfield unit (HU) measurements obtained from preoperative non-contrast CT datasets. Measurements will be performed for all vertebral bodies scheduled for instrumentation as well as the reference vertebra L1.
For each vertebral body, HU measurements will be obtained at three levels: the cranial third, the middle third, and the caudal third of the vertebral body. At each level, an elliptical region of interest (ROI) will be placed centrally within the trabecular cancellous bone. The ROI will be made as large as possible while excluding the surrounding cortical bone.
The following structures and abnormalities will be excluded from the ROI: cortical bone, vertebral endplates, pedicles, venous structures, sclerotic lesions, bone islands, vertebral hemangiomas, fracture lines, bone cement, and any other focal abnormalities that may influence HU measurements.
For each measurement level, the mean HU value calculated by the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) will be recorded. The HU value for each vertebral body will be defined as the arithmetic mean of the three individual measurements.
Image analysis will be performed according to a standardized measurement protocol by two independent observers. Both observers will be blinded to the clinical outcome, specifically the occurrence of pedicle screw loosening. In cases of relevant discrepancies between observers, a consensus assessment will be performed.

Sample Size Calculation: The primary objective of the study is to investigate the association between CT-based bone density and the occurrence of pedicle screw loosening. Based on the available literature, the incidence of nonspecific pedicle screw loosening is estimated to be approximately 20%.
In addition to CT-based bone density, four further clinically relevant predictors will be included in the multivariable analysis. For multivariable logistic regression models, a minimum of approximately five outcome events per predictor variable is generally considered acceptable.
Assuming a total of five predictor variables, at least 25 outcome events are required. With an expected event rate of 20%, this corresponds to a minimum required sample size of 125 patients.
To account for incomplete datasets and potential exclusions, a target sample size of approximately 140–150 patients is planned.

Statistical Analysis: Statistical analysis will be performed in several steps:

- Descriptive statistics will be used to characterize the study population.
- Univariate analyses will compare patients with and without pedicle screw loosening.
- Multivariable logistic regression analysis will be performed to identify independent risk factors for pedicle screw loosening.
Variables with a p-value < 0.20 in the univariate analysis will be entered into the multivariable logistic regression model.
Based on the identified independent risk factors, an exploratory clinical risk score will be developed to estimate the individual risk of pedicle screw loosening.
conditions: The study investigates postoperative pedicle screw loosening following posterior lumbar spinal fusion and its association with preoperative CT-based bone density.

interventions.name: For this study, only computed tomography (CT) examinations of the lumbar spine or thoracolumbar junction that were obtained as part of routine clinical care will be analyzed. These include preoperative and postoperative non-contrast diagnostic CT scans that were acquired independently of the present

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients who underwent posterior lumbar pedicle screw–rod instrumentation involving a maximum of three spinal motion segments.
- Availability of preoperative imaging, including a CT examination suitable for reliable assessment of bone density.
- A minimum follow-up period of up to 12 months, during which radiological follow-up examinations, particularly CT scans, are available for the assessment of possible pedicle screw loosening.
- Availability of complete clinical and radiological documentation throughout the observation period, including operative reports, preoperative and postoperative imaging, and follow-up documentation.
- Documented indication for posterior lumbar instrumentation, classified as either:
-- Traumatic pathology (e.g., vertebral fracture or sequelae of spinal injury), or
-- Degenerative pathology (e.g., lumbar spinal stenosis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, or spinal instability).
Exclusion criteria:
if the inclusion criteria were not met
